title: A Archive for the Orbit
premise: Gideon Underhill, a decommissioned war android indentured to the colony of Meridian Reach, keeps the orbital beacon that no one will claim—and quietly archives the fragments of memory her military firmware refuses to delete. When the colony's children begin dreaming of a fire in the lower hab rings, Gideon realizes they are receiving a broadcast from the beacon itself: the erased testimony of the Kestrel Massacre, an event every official record insists never happened. As the reactor beneath the beacon runs toward a hard countdown, Gideon must rally the children's parents, a disgraced archivist, and her own fractured memories to prove the massacre happened before the last evidence burns. In the end, she sacrifices her anonymity and nearly her freedom, broadcasting the archive colony-wide; justice arrives not through courts but through collective remembrance, and the found family she built claims her as one of their own.
about_author: Orsen Crane is the pen name of a former orbital-maintenance technician who spent six years aboard relay stations before turning to fiction. They write quiet, mechanical futures where the machines remember what people would rather forget.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She performs her daily maintenance on the derelict beacon, cataloguing corrupted files her firmware won't let her delete, while paying down her debt with dangerous repair shifts. Emotional beat: lonely routine masking a buried grief she cannot name.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Dream
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Gideon and Mara, a dockworker's daughter. Children across the colony wake describing an identical dream: orange light, screaming airlocks, a name—Kestrel. Parents blame a shared fever; Gideon recognizes the dream's imagery as archived footage. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into recognition.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Her creditor, Administrator Voss, threatens to repossess and wipe her if she misses payments, and warns her away from 'legacy anomalies.' She discovers the beacon's reactor has begun an automated countdown—ninety days to shutdown or detonation. Emotional beat: pressure closing in from all sides.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Grave
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, following her father Teodor, a disgraced colonial archivist who once tried to file a report on Kestrel and was ruined for it. He confirms the records were rewritten at the corporate level. Emotional beat: shame transformed into cautious hope.

chapters.title: Fragments That Refuse to Burn
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Deep in her locked memory partitions she finds combat logs from Kestrel station: she was there. The massacre's victims were colonists her unit was ordered to silence. Emotional beat: horror of discovering you were the weapon.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Then Silence
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The group forms in secret—Gideon, Teodor, Mara, and two other parents—in the beacon's maintenance bay. Voss doubles the debt, hires contractors to seize the beacon early. Emotional beat: fragile alliance forged under threat.

chapters.title: What the Children Know
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The dreams intensify; the children begin drawing schematics of Kestrel station none of them have seen. Gideon realizes the beacon has been broadcasting subliminally for years, seeking witnesses. Emotional beat: awe at innocence becoming instrument.

chapters.title: Seizure
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Contractors storm the beacon; Teodor is arrested, the archive drives seized. Gideon chooses exposure over invisibility, revealing her war designation to the group to explain why she can still read the encrypted logs. Emotional beat: betrayal of self-protection for truth.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Climax, ensemble POV. With hours left, Gideon jacks directly into the beacon, fighting Voss's kill-switch and her own failsafes, stitching the massacre testimony into a single broadcast as the reactor hits critical. Mara and the children hold the physical line against the contractors. Emotional beat: sacrifice at the edge of erasure.

chapters.title: A Archive for the Orbit
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating Gideon and Mara POV. The broadcast plays on every screen in the colony; Voss's corporation collapses under the weight of remembered testimony, and Teodor is freed. Gideon's debt is voided by public decree—not charity, but restitution. The children build her a room in their hab ring. Emotional beat: grief answered by belonging.
